title: Update documentation with common settings universities may want to set
description:
## Context
As more universities onboard onto Positron Server, let's update the documentation with more FAQs and common settings they may want to configure when using Positron Server with large classrooms

## AC
1. To have students route directly to Positron on launch and bypass the JupyterHub landing page, please use the following setting: 
From: c.Spawner.default_url = '/lab'
To: c.Spawner.default_url = '/positron'
https://jupyterhub.readthedocs.io/en/5.2.1/reference/config-reference.html

https://discourse.jupyter.org/t/changing-default-tab-when-jupyterlab-starts/7808/8
https://jupyterhub.readthedocs.io/en/5.2.1/reference/config-reference.html

Claude assisted recommendations: 

2. Startup time for Positron Server 
Positron Server can take longer to initialize than a plain Jupyter kernel, especially on the first launch of a term or on modestly sized instances. The JupyterHub defaults (30s HTTP timeout, 60s start timeout).  We may want to give recommendations on wat to update the following settings to

```
c.Spawner.http_timeout = 60
c.Spawner.start_timeout = 90
```

3. Prepare for login rush of multiple users 

When 40+ students all log in at the start of a lab session, JupyterHub can reject a burst of simultaneous spawns. Tune these so the rush doesn't 429:

```
c.JupyterHub.concurrent_spawn_limit = 40   # default is 100; lower if your host is resource constrained, raise if it can handle bursts
c.JupyterHub.active_server_limit = 0
```

4. Free resources from idle sessions

Positron sessions may sit open and idle between office hours or homework sessions. If you're on shared infrastructure, register the idle culler as a service so abandoned servers get reaped automatically:

```
c.JupyterHub.services = [
    {
        "name": "idle-culler",
        "admin": True,
        "command": [
            "python3", "-m", "jupyterhub_idle_culler",
            "--timeout=3600",       # cull after 1 hour idle
            "--cull-every=300",
        ],
    },
    # ... your positron-license service from the Get Started guide ...
]
```


5. We may want to call out that Positron uses more memory and ram than RStudio. 
Resource limits. We should recommend resource guarantee/ cap to prevent on runaway Positron session from starving everyone esle.
Sample settings to tune: 
```
c.Spawner.mem_limit = '2G'
c.Spawner.cpu_limit = 1
```

6. We may want to call out some useful Positron admin settings like `ai.enabled = false`, `extensions.autoUpdate:false` or route to the specific doc https://positron.posit.co/ai-configuration.html#turn-features-on-or-off. 

https://posit-dev.github.io/jupyter-positron-server/configuration.html#admin-enforced-settings

title: Add Dockerfile example for JupyterHub deployments
description:
The current get started docs walk through downloading and untarring Positron Server manually, but most JupyterHub deployments manage software via Docker images. It would be helpful to include a documented Dockerfile snippet (or a minimal example image) that admins can drop into their build, covering:

- Architecture-aware download from the CDN
- Extracting the binary to a standard path
- Placing the license file

This would also give us a natural place to pin a tested Positron Server version alongside a given jupyter-positron-server release, so users have a clear reference for what version pair is known to work.

title: Provide a one-time admin install script
description:
Setting up Positron Server requires several manual steps that are easy to get wrong — picking the right architecture URL, untarring to the right location, making sure it ends up on PATH. An install-positron-server.sh script in the repo (linked from docs) would make this a single command for admins, and could handle:


- Auto-detecting architecture (x86_64 vs aarch64)
- Downloading the correct tarball from the CDN
- Extracting to a configurable target directory (default e.g. /opt/positron-server)
- Printing next steps for license placement

This keeps the install explicit and auditable (no silent downloads at runtime) while meaningfully reducing the setup friction. It could also serve as the foundation for the update flow in #14.

title: Surface Positron Server startup errors (e.g. missing license) in JH UI
description:
noted in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/13123

> Ideally a warning about the license would somehow surface

When Positron Server fails to start due to a missing or invalid license file, right now you'll have to go to the logs for more info since you'll only get a "failed to start in time" error. Startup errors from Positron Server (e.g. license not found) should be caught by `jupyter-positron-server` and surfaced to the user in the JH UI using the standard JupyterLab UI helpers.

We'll want to add in the TypeScript [JupyterLab apputils](https://jupyterlab.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/modules/apputils.html), eg, something like:

```typescript
import { showErrorMessage } from '@jupyterlab/apputils';

showErrorMessage(
  'Positron Server failed to start',
  'A valid license file was not found. Set the POSITRON_LICENSE_KEY_FILE ' +
  'environment variable to the path of your license file.\n\n' +
  'Request a free academic license at academic-licenses@posit.co or see the ' +
  'documentation: https://posit-dev.github.io/jupyter-positron-server/'
);
```


References to look at later:
- JupyterLab UI helpers docs: https://jupyterlab.readthedocs.io/en/stable/extension/ui_helpers.html
- `showErrorMessage` API: https://jupyterlab.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/functions/apputils.showErrorMessage.html
- `Notification` API: https://jupyterlab.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/modules/apputils.Notification.html

title: Missing `--server-base-path` on start causes Not Found
description:
## Summary

The `positron-server` Web binary (`vscode-reh-web-linux-x64`) returns `Not found` (HTTP 404)
on all paths including `/` when started without the `--server-base-path` argument.
The `setup_positron_server()` function does not pass this argument, making Positron
Server inaccessible via `jupyter-server-proxy`.

## Environment

- `jupyter-positron-server`: 0.0.2 / 0.0.3
- JupyterHub: z2jh (Zero to JupyterHub) on Kubernetes
- Base image: `quay.io/jupyter/r-notebook:lab-4.5.6`
- Positron Server binary: `positron-server-linux-x64-2026.04.0-269`
- JupyterHub `base_url`: `/jh/`
- `JUPYTERHUB_SERVICE_PREFIX`: `/jh/user/testuser/`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install and configure `jupyter-positron-server` with `positron-server` in PATH
2. Start JupyterHub single-user server
3. Click Positron in the JupyterLab launcher
4. Observe `Not found` / `504 Gateway Timeout`

Alternatively, reproduce directly in the container:

```bash
PORT=9999
TOKEN=testtoken

# Without --server-base-path (current behavior)
positron-server \
    --accept-server-license-terms \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
    --port $PORT \
    --connection-token $TOKEN \
    --license-key-file /path/to/license.lic &

sleep 10
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/?tkn=$TOKEN"
# → 404
```

## Expected Behavior

With `--server-base-path` set correctly, `positron-server` responds with HTTP 200:

```bash
# With --server-base-path (fixed behavior)
positron-server \
    --accept-server-license-terms \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
    --port $PORT \
    --connection-token $TOKEN \
    --server-base-path /jh/user/testuser/positron \
    --license-key-file /path/to/license.lic &

sleep 10
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
    "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/jh/user/testuser/positron/?tkn=$TOKEN"
# → 200
```

## Root Cause

`setup_positron_server()` does not include `--server-base-path` in the command arguments.
The comment in the code suggests this was intentionally omitted in favour of
`X-Forwarded-Prefix`, but the Positron Web Server requires `--server-base-path` to
serve any content at all.

```python
# Current code – missing --server-base-path
command_arguments = [
    "--accept-server-license-terms",
    "--host", host,
    "--port", "{port}",
    "--connection-token", _CONNECTION_TOKEN,
]
```

## Proposed Fix

Pass `--server-base-path` dynamically from the JupyterHub environment variable
`JUPYTERHUB_SERVICE_PREFIX`:

```python
import os

service_prefix = os.environ.get("JUPYTERHUB_SERVICE_PREFIX", "/").rstrip("/")
server_base_path = service_prefix + "/positron"

command_arguments = [
    "--accept-server-license-terms",
    "--host", host,
    "--port", "{port}",
    "--connection-token", _CONNECTION_TOKEN,
    "--server-base-path", server_base_path,
]
```

`JUPYTERHUB_SERVICE_PREFIX` is automatically set by JupyterHub in every
single-user server environment (e.g. `/jh/user/testuser/`), so this works
generically without hardcoding any paths.

## Notes

- This bug only affects the **web** binary (`positron-server-*` /
  `vscode-reh-web-linux-x64`).
- `X-Forwarded-Prefix` alone is not sufficient – `--server-base-path` is required
  for `positron-server` to serve any HTTP response other than `Not found`.

title: `mappath` pattern does not support JupyterHub `base_url` prefix
description:
from external user

## Summary

The `mappath` regex pattern in `_make_mappath()` only matches paths starting with
`/user/USERNAME/positron/` but fails when JupyterHub is deployed under a custom
`base_url` prefix (e.g. `/jh/`). This results in a `Not found` error when clicking
the Positron launcher entry in JupyterLab.

Additionally, the pattern requires a trailing slash after `positron` which causes
a `404` on the initial request (without trailing slash) before the redirect adds it.

## Environment

- `jupyter-positron-server`: 0.0.2 / 0.0.3
- JupyterHub: z2jh (Zero to JupyterHub) on Kubernetes
- Base image: `quay.io/jupyter/r-notebook:lab-4.5.6`
- Positron Server: `positron-server-linux-x64-2026.04.0-269`
- JupyterHub `base_url`: `/jh/` (configured via `hub.baseUrl` in `values.yaml`)
- Positron Server: `positron-server-linux-x64-2026.04.0-269`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy JupyterHub with a custom `base_url`, e.g. `/jh/`
2. Install and configure `jupyter-positron-server`
3. Click the Positron launcher entry in JupyterLab

## Error

Browser shows `Not found` when navigating to:
```
https://your-hub.example.com/jh/user/testuser/positron/?tkn=<token>
```

Debug output from `mappath`:
```
mappath: /jh/user/testuser/positron/ (no match)
```

## Root Cause

The pattern in `_make_mappath()` does not account for a `base_url` prefix:

```python
# Current (buggy) pattern
pattern = re.compile(r"^/user/[^/]+/positron(/.*)$")
```

**Problem 1:** Does not match `/jh/user/testuser/positron/` because of the `/jh` prefix.

**Problem 2:** Requires a trailing slash – does not match `/jh/user/testuser/positron`
(without trailing slash), which is the URL of the initial request before the
`302` redirect adds the trailing slash.

Test results with current pattern:
```
/jh/user/testuser/positron      → NO MATCH  ← initial request fails
/jh/user/testuser/positron/     → NO MATCH  ← after redirect, still fails
/user/testuser/positron/        → /          ← works (no prefix)
```

## Expected Behavior

The pattern should match both with and without a `base_url` prefix, and with or
without a trailing slash:

```
/jh/user/testuser/positron      → /
/jh/user/testuser/positron/     → /
/jh/user/testuser/positron/foo  → /foo
/user/testuser/positron/        → /
```

## Proposed Fix

```python
# Fixed pattern – base_url prefix optional, trailing slash optional
pattern = re.compile(r"^(?:/jh)?/user/[^/]+/positron(/?.*)?$")
```

Or more generically to support any `base_url` prefix, read it from the
JupyterHub environment variable:

```python
import os
base_url = os.environ.get("JUPYTERHUB_BASE_URL", "").rstrip("/")
pattern = re.compile(
    rf"^(?:{re.escape(base_url)})?/user/[^/]+/positron(/?.*)?$"
)
```

The generic solution is preferred as it works for any `base_url` configuration
without hardcoding `/jh/`.

title: `which_positron_server()` returns relative string instead of full path
description:
report from external use

## Summary

`which_positron_server()` returns the string `"positron-server"` (relative) instead of the
full absolute path when the binary is found via `which()`. This causes `os.path.realpath()`
to resolve the path relative to the current working directory (`/home/jovyan`) instead of
the actual binary location, leading to a wrong `activation_path` and a `FileNotFoundError`.

## Environment

- `jupyter-positron-server`: 0.0.2 / 0.0.3
- JupyterHub: z2jh (Zero to JupyterHub) on Kubernetes
- Base image: `quay.io/jupyter/r-notebook:lab-4.5.6`
- Positron Server: `positron-server-linux-x64-2026.04.0-269`
- Binary installed at: `/opt/vscode-reh-web-linux-x64/bin/positron-server`
- Binary added to `PATH` via `ENV` in Dockerfile

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install `positron-server` binary to a custom path (e.g. `/opt/vscode-reh-web-linux-x64/bin/`)
2. Add that path to `PATH` via Dockerfile `ENV`
3. Install `jupyter-positron-server`
4. Start JupyterHub single-user server and click Positron in the JupyterLab launcher

## Error

```
FileNotFoundError: Positron activation libraries not found at '/home/jovyan/resources/activation/linux/x86_64'.
This usually means positron-server is not installed correctly for your architecture (x86_64).
Expected directory structure: /home/resources/activation/linux/x86_64/
```

## Root Cause

In `which_positron_server()`, the `which()` check returns `True` but the function
returns the bare string `"positron-server"` instead of the resolved path:

```python
# Current (buggy) code
if which(prog):
    return prog  # ← returns "positron-server" (relative!)
```

Subsequently in `setup_positron_server()`:

```python
positron_server_path = which_positron_server()   # → "positron-server"
real_path = os.path.realpath(positron_server_path)
# os.path.realpath("positron-server") resolves relative to CWD (/home/jovyan)
# → "/home/jovyan/positron-server" (wrong!)
positron_root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(real_path))
# → "/home/jovyan" (wrong!)
activation_path = os.path.join(positron_root, "resources", "activation", "linux", arch)
# → "/home/jovyan/resources/activation/linux/x86_64" (wrong!)
```

## Expected Behavior

`which_positron_server()` should return the full absolute path to the binary:

```python
# Fixed code
if which(prog):
    return which(prog)  # ← returns "/opt/vscode-reh-web-linux-x64/bin/positron-server"
```

## Proposed Fix

```python
# In which_positron_server():
if which(prog):
    return which(prog)  # Return full path instead of bare string
```

This ensures `os.path.realpath()` resolves correctly regardless of the
current working directory.

title: look in more locations for the license
description:
from pairing with @testlabauto 

---

Right now, we automatically look into `POSITRON_LICENSE_KEY_FILE` envvar and `opt/license.lic` for a license, but that doesn't seem quite comprehensive enough.

I think it would be reasonable to look inside the `/opt/positron-server/` directory for a license as well. Additionally, we should look for `positron.lic` instead of just `license.lic`.



It might be helpful to have a small docs section on the Getting Started page dedicated just to license placement, since everything will fail quite dramatically if it isn't set as expected 😅

title: Improve the update process
description: At the moment, updating Positron Server includes replaying the entire install process. It would be way nicer to have an auto-update feature or at least a documented script to replace in-place so folks don't lose access to settings, etc.

title: Create installation helper skill
description: One way to help people install Positron + JupyterHub would be to have a skill agents could use (perhaps in this repo)? We could really tailor it to the happy installation path, potential gotchas, etc, so users could be set up for success if they're using agentic support for an install

title: Should this package handle installation of Positron Server?
description:
The steps for getting started include downloading Positron manually from the CDN. It's a bit clunky, and it would be nice if this package could handle this task. 

There's a lot of benefits for owning the whole process, including discovery of Positron Server. We'd want to make sure the path is configurable, and then pass it along to the startup sequence. It'd probably be a nice base for starting on a better flow for updating Positron (besides, reinstall a new version of Positron Server).

title: Open Positron in same workspace as active in JupyterHub
description: right now, Positron just launches from the root folder of the server. We want to remember where folks are at in JupyterLab, eg, if they're working in a certain workspace, and then launch that same workspace in Positron.
